title: Voyager Crossed an Invisible Border
description: How scientists used plasma vibrations to confirm Voyager 1 had entered interstellar space. NASA imagery includes artist concepts, labeled on screen. #Voyager #Space #Science
fact_text: This probe crossed a border no camera could see. NASA launched Voyager One in 1977. Decades later, it reached the edge of the Sun's enormous bubble of charged particles. But how could anyone tell it had crossed? There was no finish line floating in space. The clue came from the gas around it. A burst from the Sun made that gas vibrate. Voyager measured those vibrations, and scientists used them to work out the gas's density. It was far denser than the gas inside the bubble. That was evidence of interstellar space. Looking back through the data, the team traced the crossing to August 2012. A spacecraft from the seventies had found an invisible border by measuring the space around it.

sources.title: NASA: Voyager enters interstellar space
sources.claim: Voyager 1 launched in 1977; plasma-wave measurements and earlier particle data placed its crossing into interstellar space in August 2012.
